layman_headline: Market rallied hard this week — waiting for a pullback before jumping in.
layman_explanation: Almost every major cryptocurrency surged 15-30% in the past week. That's exciting, but buying after a big run-up is risky — prices often pull back before continuing higher. The swing trade candidates are either already extended (PUMP up 54%, ZEC up 42%, HYPE up 30%) or are stablecoins that don't move. Bitcoin dominance at 59.3% also signals that altcoins face headwinds. The smartest move right now is patience.
layman_action: Stay in cash and wait. Set alerts for ETH around $2,350 and SOL around $88 — if prices pull back 5-8%, those would be much better entry points with defined risk.
expert_reasoning: The entire market just moved 15-30% in one week. Every swing candidate has negative composite scores driven by extended 7-day price action. BTC dominance at 59.3% is hostile for altcoin entries. Fear & Greed at 65 (down from 74 yesterday) suggests momentum is already cooling — a healthy pullback is likely before the next leg. Without RSI, MACD, or volume data on the candidates, and with all signals showing 'may be extended,' chasing here violates core swing trading discipline. ETH is the strongest large-cap setup on a pullback given its DeFi dominance and news catalysts.
risk_factors: Higher US PCE inflation data already pushing BTC below $78K — macro headwinds could trigger a deeper correction than expected
BTC dominance at 59.3% may continue rising, further pressuring altcoin performance
No RSI/MACD data available on candidates makes it impossible to properly time entries
watch_list: BTC price action around $76K-$78K support — a break below could cascade into altcoins
ETH price behavior near $2,350-$2,400 for a potential pullback entry zone
Fear & Greed index trend — if it drops from 65 toward 50, that creates better buying conditions
market_context: The crypto market just experienced a massive weekly rally (BTC +14.7%, ETH +18.2%, XRP +29.2%) but is now cooling off with BTC dipping below $78K on hot inflation data. High BTC dominance at 59.3% and a declining Fear & Greed index suggest caution on new altcoin entries.
context_banner: Post-rally consolidation phase — discipline demands waiting for a pullback rather than chasing extended moves.

key_signals.description: Fear & Greed dropped from 74 to 65 in one day, signaling momentum exhaustion after the weekly rally — wait for further cooling.
Bitcoin dipped below $78K on higher US PCE inflation data, introducing macro headwinds that could trigger broader pullbacks.
No volume data available on swing candidates and all show 7-day moves of +25-54%, suggesting they are chasing rather than setting up fresh breakouts.
Dallas Fed warning on tokenized deposits stripping $700B from banks and Ethereum quantum-resistance proposals provide longer-term fundamental context for ETH.
Ethereum DeFi TVL remains dominant at $49B, confirming its fundamental strength — but best entered on a pullback, not after an 18% weekly run.
